## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py`'s integration verification (`_integrate_into_dev` /
`verifyIntegration`, SA-0MT456M27001LRTL) creates a fresh worktree with
`git worktree add --detach <path> <dev_sha>` and then runs `npm run build` in
it. `git worktree add` never populates git submodules, so any repository that
vendors a submodule builds against an **empty** submodule directory in the
integration worktree.

The build then fails with a module-resolution error, the audit marks any
execution-dependent AC (e.g. "Build and full test suite pass") as `partial`,
and the item's verdict is "Ready to close: No" — a **false negative**: the
real, populated checkout builds and tests green.

## Precedent (the fix already exists for implement worktrees)

`implement.py start` was fixed to populate submodules in new worktrees:
**SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ** (completed) added `_ensure_submodules(worktree_path,
repo_root)` running `git submodule update --init --recursive`, fail-open with a
warning. The audit skill's integration worktree should apply the same pattern;
today it does not.

Related: **SA-0MW4ZRLSI005PHL6** (open) — audit should run its pipeline in a
fresh worktree at latest `origin/dev`; this item covers the submodule
population that fresh-worktree execution needs.

## Evidence (2026-11-08, tce-the-rising)

- Audit of `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` AC4: "Build fails (exit code 2) but errors
  are … missing vite config modules, **not from this item's changes**". The
  audit recognises the failure is environmental yet still blocks.
- On the real (populated) tree, `npm run build` exits **0**; the cached full
  suite is green.
- `vite.config.ts` imports from `./core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin`
  and `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin`; `core/` is a tracked submodule.
- `git -c submodule.recurse=true worktree add --detach <tmp> <sha>` leaves
  `core/` with **0** entries (git 2.53.0) — `worktree add` does not recurse
  into submodules.
- `audit_runner.py` contains no `git submodule update --init` call.

## Desired change

After creating the integration worktree (and before `npm run build`), populate
tracked submodules — reuse/extract the `_ensure_submodules` helper pattern from
`implement.py` (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ). Fail-open: a repo with no submodules must
be unaffected, and a submodule-init failure logs a warning without aborting the
audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The integration worktree used by `audit_runner.py` has its tracked
      submodules populated before `npm run build` (verified on a repo with a
      submodule dependency: the submodule directory is non-empty).
- [ ] `npm run build` in the integration worktree succeeds on a tree that
      builds green in the main checkout, so execution-dependent ACs are not
      marked `partial` for the empty-submodule reason.
- [ ] A repo without submodules is unaffected (fail-open); a submodule-init
      failure warns and does not abort the audit.
- [ ] A regression test covers the submodule-population step.

## Impact

Audits of build-dependent items on any submodule-vendoring repository reflect
the real tree, and releases stop being blocked by false-negative "not ready to
close" verdicts.

## Context

Discovered during the 2026-11-08 `/skill:ship release` of tce-the-rising, which
was blocked at the audit gate on `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` for this reason. The
per-project item filed there (`RISE-0MW7YP6SD0091MKJ`) is superseded by this
generic framework item and will be deleted.

## Problem statement

During an audit, `audit_runner.py` transitions the target item out of
`completed`/`in_review` (to `in-progress`/`in_review` or `open`/`plan_complete`)
and is supposed to **restore it to `completed`/`in_review`** on every exit path
(the abort path logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring "completed" "in_review"`).

Under concurrency this restore is **lost**: a `wl sync` running in another
session (or the audit runner's own sync) races the restore, and the item is
left stuck at `open`/`plan_complete` (status `open`, stage `plan_complete`,
`auditResult: null`). The item silently drops out of the release candidate set
(`stage: in_review`) and looks like brand-new, un-implemented work — a
**worklog data-integrity regression**, not a cosmetic glitch.

This is the same class as the known concurrent-`wl sync` lost-update race
(WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ); the audit runner's own status restore is not
race-safe against it.

## Observed (2026-11-08, tce-the-rising `/skill:ship release`)

A single release attempt corrupted **four** items, each left at
`open`/`plan_complete` although all four were `completed`/`in_review` before:

| Item | Corrupted by | Prior state (from worklog-data history) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RISE-0MVWWBT8Y009FMZ6` | release gate audit remediation (14:00) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3MXVU5009GMLR` | `--refresh-audits` (14:38) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:57) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:59) | `completed`/`in_review` |

All four were repaired by hand (`wl update <id> --status completed --stage
in_review`) after reconstructing the prior state from the `refs/worklog/...`
delta history. The corruption spans both the failing-verdict path (a
persisted "Ready to close: No" still left the item at `open`/`plan_complete`)
and the aborted path (the "restoring" message logged but the restore did not
persist).

## Root-cause hypotheses to confirm

- The restore is a plain `wl update` with no compare-and-swap / version guard,
  so a concurrent `wl sync` (pull→merge→push) overwrites it (last-writer-wins
  on a stale snapshot).
- A failing/aborted audit may not run the restore at all on some exit paths
  (the observed `open`/`plan_complete` with a persisted failing verdict
  suggests the restore is skipped when the verdict is not "Yes").

## Desired change

Make the audit runner's status restore **race-safe and unconditional**:

- Restore `completed`/`in_review` on **every** exit path — success, failing
  verdict, abort, exception, timeout — via `try/finally`.
- Use the shared `StatusLifecycle` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  and its claim/assignee handling so the restore participates in the same
  lost-update protection as other lifecycle exits.
- Guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (e.g. re-read after write,
  retry on mismatch — the same verification pattern the ship skill uses for
  close verification, SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- Never leave an item at `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed
  — a failing verdict is recorded while the item stays `completed`/`in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A failing audit verdict (Ready to close: No) leaves the item at
      `completed`/`in_review` with the verdict persisted — never `open`/`plan_complete`.
- [ ] An aborted audit (timeout / parse failure / provider error) restores the
      item to `completed`/`in_review`; the restore is verified after write and
      retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered it.
- [ ] The restore runs on every exit path (`try/finally`), including exceptions.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` (or a stale-snapshot
      write) between the audit's status change and its restore, and asserts the
      item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] No item is left at `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect of any audit
      path.

## Impact

Auditing an `in_review` item can no longer silently revert it to un-implemented
work, so release candidate sets and worklog state stay correct under
concurrent agent sessions.

## Context

Discovered during the 2026-11-08 `/skill:ship release` of tce-the-rising (four
items corrupted and repaired by hand). Related: the concurrent-`wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ) and the ship close-verification pattern
(SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).

## Problem

The audit runner's in-main-slot resume clears its own view of pending child screens but does not delete the on-disk signal file.

Observed on 2026-11-09 auditing `CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE` (Tableau-Card-Engine):

- Run 1 (12:09-12:11) emitted one in-main-slot child screen for `CG-0MW97UZ68001JTGK` and wrote `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE.pending-screens.json`.
- The child was then closed (duplicate, failure fixed upstream).
- Resume run (13:33-13:34) reported `"pending_child_screens": []` in its JSON and a `Ready to close: Yes` verdict, **but the signal file was still present afterwards**, still naming the closed child.

## Impact

`cmd_issue` bypasses the freshness gate while `pending-screens.json` names any child (SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S). A stale file therefore forces every later audit of that item to re-run the whole Phase 1 pipeline (one model call each) even though nothing is pending — a silent, repeatable cost. The document says the signal 'is cleared automatically when no screens remain'; it is not.

## Reproduction

1. Audit an item with one unaudited child in default in-main-slot mode to get the pending signal written.
2. Persist/close the child so no screens remain, then re-run the parent audit.
3. Observe `pending_child_screens: []` in the JSON while `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/<id>.pending-screens.json` still lists the child.

## Expected

The signal file is removed (or rewritten empty and then removed) whenever the collected pending set is empty, on both the fresh-run and resume paths.

## Actual

The file persists with its previous content.

## Workaround applied

Deleted the stale file manually so the next audit can take the freshness fast path.

## Discovered from

CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE (Tableau-Card-Engine docs audit)

# Bug — a matched changed-scope group silently drops other changed test files

discovered-from:SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40 (driving the parent AC4 test gap exposed it).

## Problem

`changed_scope_selection()` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) resolves a
declared test **group** first and returns immediately:

```python
group_name = select_group_from_changed_files(changed, root)
if group_name is not None:
    group_cmds = group_commands(group_name, root)
    if group_cmds:
        return ChangedScopeSelection(list(group_cmds), ...)
```

When a change set touches **both** a path matched by a group (`paths`) and a
test file the group does not cover, the group's command replaces the file-level
selection instead of unioning with it. The edit-authored test file is then
silently absent from the changed-scope run.

### Observed (SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40)

Changed files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` → matches the `implement` group
  (`skill/implement/**`) → command `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings
  skill/implement/tests/`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` (the file the run was verifying) → **dropped**

Result: `212 passed`, none of them the two newly added tests. Running with only
the test file changed selected it correctly (`212 passed` including the new
tests), so the loss is specific to the group short-circuit.

## Impact

A changed-scope run now executes every test file the change set touches — including an
edit-authored test outside a matched test group — so a green changed-scope run
actually includes the new tests instead of reporting success without running them.
(Before the fix a green run could pass while never executing the tests the author
just wrote; the dev-push full-suite gate was the only backstop.)

## Acceptance criteria

1. A selection where a group matches *and* other changed test files exist emits
   the group's commands **unioned** with the file-level selection (deduplicated,
   deterministic order), or fails closed to the full suite — never silently
   drops a changed test file.
2. A test pins the union (changed source under a group path + changed test file
   outside the group's directories); the emitted command lists both.
3. A test pins that a group-only match still emits exactly the group command
   (no behaviour change for the single-match case).
4. `run_tests.py --scope changed` on a change set containing
   `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` + `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
   selects `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.
5. Changed-scope tests pass; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.


## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `changed_scope_selection()` short-circuits
  on a matched group (the bug); `select_group_from_changed_files()` picks the
  group; `_commands_for_selected_tests()` builds the file-level commands and
  `group_commands()` resolves the group's declared commands.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — changed-scope selection tests
  (`TestChangedScopeGroups`); the union + group-only regression tests (AC2/AC3)
  belong here.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_run_group_from_changed_files()` is
  a second, redundant group-first short-circuit: `_run_resolved_suite()` returns
  its result before `changed_scope_selection()` is consulted. See OPEN QUESTION.

## Test-first ordering

Write the failing union tests (AC2/AC3) first and confirm they reproduce the
drop against the current `changed_scope_selection()`, then fix. After the fix
the changed-scope run (AC4) must list `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.

## Suggested approach

1. In `changed_scope_selection()`, when a group matches, also resolve the
   file-level selection for changed test files **not** covered by the matched
   group's `paths`, then return the union: group commands first (declared
   order), then file-level commands (sorted), deduplicated. Keep the
   single-match (group-only) case byte-identical (AC3).
2. If the union cannot be constructed safely, fail closed to the full suite
   rather than dropping a changed test file (AC1).

## OPEN QUESTION

Is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_run_group_from_changed_files()` in
scope for this item, or deferred to SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9 (changed-scope group
union + selector convergence, AC3)?

- Why it matters: fixing only `changed_scope_selection()` leaves the implement
  `finish` gate — the path this bug was observed through — still short-circuiting
  on the redundant group-first selector, so the same silent drop recurs there.
- Recommendation: converge the finish gate on `changed_scope_selection()` in the
  same change (it already honours groups, so the extra selector is dead
  duplication). Note that `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_groups.py::
  test_implement_has_group_runner` asserts the function exists and must be
  updated if it is removed.

### Goal
Add check-filing subcommand to intake.py and wire it as step 0c after claim. Add CLI flags for misfiled-item handling.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. skill:intake runs a filing-location check for the target work item before any other mutation, and reports its findings to the operator (stderr plus work-item comment). The check is non-blocking: intake proceeds whether or not the item passes the check.
2. On a non-ok classification the script logs a warning and records an idempotent filing location check comment on the item (re-runs update the existing comment, never duplicate). When stdin is an interactive TTY it additionally offers continue or recreate the item in the correct project. Auto-recreation is only possible via an explicit --misfiled-action recreate flag and never happens by default.
3. Recreating (when chosen) creates a new item under the target project's store/prefix copying title, description, tags, issue type and priority, records a Recreated from source-id reference, and closes the original with the reason Misfiled: recreated in target-project (target-id). A dry-run --dry-run mode prints the would-be recreation without creating.
4. intake.py gains a check-filing <id> subcommand that runs the filing check.
5. check-filing runs as step 0c right after claim in the intake flow.
6. CLI gains --misfiled-action {warn,offer,recreate} (default warn), --recreate-target <project-dir>, and --dry-run flags.
7. No other skill's behavior changes in this work item.
8. The check is non-blocking - intake proceeds whether or not the item passes.
9. Idempotent - re-running the check on the same item yields the same result and never duplicates comments or recreations.

# Remote-observed push verdict in finish

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Builds on the test-first slice (the hermetic baselines land first; this slice makes them pass
and removes their `xfail(strict=True)` markers).

## Goal

As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but `origin/dev`
already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the completion comment and leave the
item `completed`/`in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`; and as the producer, when
`finish` does report a push failure I want the report to say whether the commit was verified
**absent** from `origin/dev` or whether verification itself could not run, so I know exactly
what recovery is needed.

## Context

`git_push_to_dev()` (`implement.py` L5629) spawns `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in
its own process group. On `TimeoutExpired` it process-group-kills the push and raises
`PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` for
non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns `False`. There is
no post-failure remote check. `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
`RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on `PushTimeoutError`,
and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets the status to `open`; steps 6a–8 (post-push
ancestry assertion, cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync) and the
`StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit run only after a successful push.
`_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) retries the push inside the worktree and has the
same false-failure exposure.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`: resolve the
   full hash, read `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the
   tip differs (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the commit
   is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe itself failed
   (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape: have
   `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed" signal (or return an
   outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`, so `phase_finish` can mark
   `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and continue on the success path;
   `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment, worktree
   retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the existing post-*success* ancestry assertion
   `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084, SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U, now completed) reuses it
   rather than shipping a second divergent probe; note the reuse on both items.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629), `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050), `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084); new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper.
- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — the baselines from the test-first slice.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — interrupted-push coverage.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the annotation noting the fake must keep resolving a published commit.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was not observed on `origin/dev`; do not weaken the terminal-status read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The hook runs the full suite (~minutes); verification uses `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`merge-base` only and is bounded (recommended ~60 s). A verification fetch updates only remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit is landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev` tip. Resolve the short hash from `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal push step); the verified-landed marker is a new optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish` selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` picks it up only after `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared remote-verification probe.** A new `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout) -> bool | None` helper in `implement.py` resolves the full hash (resolving the short hash returned by `git_get_commit_hash()`), reads `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetches that ref when the tip differs (bounded, ~60 s), and returns `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>` reports the commit reachable, `False` when positively absent, and `None` when the probe itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
- **Remote-observed verdict before any failure report.** Before `finish` reports a push failure (`PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward), every non-success outcome is routed through the probe — including the non-fast-forward retry push in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` — and the verification is time-bounded and uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite).
- **Verified landed is success, not failure.** When verification confirms the commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and marks the report explicitly (`steps.push.verified_after_failure: true` plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome stay conservative.** When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or verification itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message/report distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Ancestry, additive fields, preserved behaviour, no duplicate probe.** The commit is considered landed when it is an ancestor of the current `origin/dev` tip, never equality; the probe is extracted so the existing post-success ancestry assertion `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) reuses it instead of shipping a divergent second probe; non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry, worktree retention on genuine failure, the pre-push main-checkout mutation guard and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics keep working; and `report["steps"]["push"]` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (new keys are additive only).

Documentation slice for the remote-observed push verdict. It follows the implementation slice
so it describes the shipped behaviour (the new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` probe, the report
fields, and the three outcomes) rather than a planned one.

## Goal

As an operator or implementation agent reading the finish documentation, I want the three push
outcomes and their recovery paths stated explicitly, so I never retry completed work and never
manually push a commit that is already on `origin/dev`.

## Context

The current "Push timeout" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (L1436) says a
timeout "resets status to `open`" and posts a manual-push comment — that is exactly the false
failure this parent fixes. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` describes `finish`'s behaviour around
L329–L371 but says nothing about a push verdict being verified against the remote.

## Scope

Documentation only: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, and
any code comment the implementation slice leaves inconsistent. No behaviour change.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Push timeout" section (L1436) and the push-failure table entries.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish / push-to-dev guidance (L329–L371).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — doc-hygiene guard to re-run.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — code comments in the push-outcome handlers.

## Constraints

- Describe only behaviour that the implementation slice actually ships; no speculative or aspirational wording.
- Keep the existing document structure and cross-reference style; do not restructure unrelated sections.
- UK English, and no claim that a timeout always resets the item to `open`.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Implement branch-aware worktree creation

## Goal

Make `phase_start` branch-aware so an existing child branch no longer fails
generically with "Failed to create worktree". The branch is either reused
(identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch) or the operator gets
an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.
- `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures (`created` / `branch-exists` / `failed` verdicts), with the single `phase_start` call site updated and the source-order assertion in `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` kept satisfied.
- Reuse path: a branch whose tip is an ancestor of (or equal to) the parent branch is fast-forwarded to the parent tip with `git branch -f` and registered with `git worktree add <path> <branch>` (no `-b`); the report sets `reused_branch: true` and `branch_fast_forwarded: true|false`.
- Unsafe path: a branch carrying commits not reachable from the parent branch (or from `origin/<parent_branch>`) is never reset or reused silently; `phase_start` fails with the branch name, the unique-commit count and the exact recovery commands, and resets the item to `open`.
- A branch checked out in another worktree is reported by name and never raced.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Introduce verdict constants + `branch_exists(repo_root, branch)` (via
  `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>`) and
  `_branch_reuse_verdict(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `identical` / `fast-forwardable` / `unique-commits`, plus
  `_branch_checked_out_in_other_worktree(repo_root, branch)`.
- Change `git_worktree_add` to return the verdict string; keep the call
  prefix `git_worktree_add(branch,` so existing source-order assertions hold.
- In `phase_start` step 7, when `not resumed` and `branch_exists`: compute the
  verdict, fast-forward when safe, then register the worktree from the
  existing branch; otherwise set `report["success"] = False`,
  `report["stale_branch"] = {branch, unique_commits, recovery_commands}` and
  return after resetting status to `open`.
- Report the decision under `report["steps"]["worktree_branch"]` so `parent`
  and `drive` reports surface why a start reused a branch.

## Constraints

- Never `git branch -f`, `reset` or delete a branch that has commits absent
  from the parent branch — reuse is limited to branches with no unique
  commits.
- Do not weaken the main-checkout placement guard, stash-hygiene gate, code
  freeze gate, or parent-tracking assertion.
- Preserve `--worktree-path` override semantics and the idempotent worktree
  resume path (`_is_worktree`).
- Re-running `start` after a successful reuse must be idempotent (no second
  branch, no second worktree, no duplicate comment).

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add`, new branch helpers, `phase_start` step 7

- `phase_start` reuse / fast-forward / actionable-error behaviour.

# Implement safe branch cleanup

## Goal

Stop a failed or aborted `start` from poisoning the next `start` with a
orphaned feature branch: clean up the branch this run created, remove the
abandoned branch on `abort` when it is safe to do so, and always report what
was removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed.
- The failed-`start` cleanup also removes the worktree registration it created, so no half-created `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` directory survives the failure.
- `phase_abort` discovers the abandoned branch by prefix (`refs/heads/wl-<item-id>-*`) rather than needing the item title, deletes it with `git branch -d` semantics only when it has no unique commits, and reports `branch_removed` / `branch_retained` with the reason and the recovery command.
- A branch that carries commits not reachable from the parent branch or `origin/<parent_branch>` is retained and named in the abort report and comment — never force-deleted.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- New `_delete_branch_if_safe(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `{deleted, reason, unique_commits}` with reasons `deleted` / `not-found` /
  `unique-commits` / `checked-out-elsewhere` / `error`; unique-commit count is
  taken against both the local parent branch and `origin/<parent_branch>`.
- New `_discover_item_branches(repo_root, work_item_id)` via
  `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) "refs/heads/wl-<id>-*"`.
- Wrap the post-`git worktree add` steps of `phase_start` so a failure after
  creation removes the worktree (guarded by `_remove_worktree`) and then
  deletes the branch this run created, reporting
  `report["cleanup"] = {worktree_removed, branch_removed, reason}`.
- In `phase_abort`, after the worktree removal and before
  `_restore_repo_state`, delete each discovered item branch that is safe and
  record the outcome on the abort comment.

## Constraints

- No blind `git branch -D`: deletion is only reached when the unique-commit
  count is zero, and a branch checked out in another worktree is never
  touched.
- Cleanup failures are logged and reported, never fatal to `abort`.
- Idempotent: a second abort finds no branch and reports `not-found` without
  error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_delete_branch_if_safe`, `_discover_item_branches`, `phase_start` post-create failure path, `phase_abort`
- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite".
- Blocked by "Implement branch-aware worktree creation" (shares the branch

## Deliverables

- Guarded branch deletion helper and item-branch discovery.
- Failed-start cleanup of the worktree and the branch it created.
